In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

clean energy equity indexes are not only a good alternative investment for investors concerned about the environment, but also a good investment for investors concerned with risk management and hedging, because of the effectiveness of commodity implied volatility indexes in hedging their downside risk.

this paper contributes to the literature of the risk management of clean energy equities by considering the roles and effectiveness of the volatility indexes of major commodity markets in hedging the downside risk of the clean energy stock indexes.

the implied volatilities of the three commodities are effective in hedging the downside risk of the three clean energy equity indexes, with the crude oil implied volatility being the most effective, followed by that for gold and then silver.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the implied volatility of the three major commodities can be used as an effective hedging tool for the risk of clean-energy equity indexes.
clean energy equity indexes are negatively correlated with the implied volatility indexes of crude and gold and silver, and the latter can be used to reduce the risk of the former.
investors can hedge the downside risk in the clean energy equity markets by using commodity volatility indexes, especially the crude oil volatility index.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the volatility indexes of major crude oil, gold, and silver can be effective hedging tools for clean energy equities.
the implied volatility index of gold can be used as an effective tool to hedge the downside risks of clean energy stock index.
the hedging effectiveness of implied volatility indexes varies depending on the type of clean energy stock index.
